clue.text: Benefit seekers' activity is attractive

parts.note: a good is a benefit, as in 'for the common good'
what people seeking something are doing

explanation.surface: Claimants hunting for welfare payments are somehow made to seem appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, benefit seekers are those looking for good: GOOD + LOOKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone good-looking has a pleasing appearance, which is the plain sense of attractive.

clue.text: Vegetables their cook prepared with bagels

indicators.note: food that is prepared is chopped and rearranged, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook serves up vegetables alongside a batch of bagels.
explanation.definitionFit: Globe artichokes are edible thistle heads grown and eaten as a vegetable crop.

clue.text: Musical work by Poe ruined artist

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the name before it is jumbled

parts.note: the writer's name taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A piece of music by Edgar Allan Poe spoiled the career of a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic composition set to music for singers and orchestra.

clue.text: Trellis found in the French garret

indicators.note: one word placed in another, so the room sits inside the article

parts.note: a garret is a room in the roof

explanation.surface: A garden trellis turns up in a French attic room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' reads as where the trellis is kept; only 'in' does the work, placing the room inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips, the same structure as a garden trellis.

clue.text: Trips in with gusto when drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into another order

explanation.surface: Someone tripping over enthusiastically after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' looks like stumbling, which fits the drunk picture, but it is the noun: excursions.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short excursions or pleasure trips taken away from home.

clue.text: Still, I can't wander; I have to be brief

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their places, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: 'to be brief' asks for the short form, I've

explanation.surface: Someone explains they cannot roam about and must keep things short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'nevertheless' opening a sentence, but it is the definition: motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is not moving at all, and inactive likewise describes a thing doing nothing.

clue.text: Fetching sort of animal?

parts.note: surface reading: an attractive, appealing creature
setter's reading: a dog breed known for fetching shot game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' usually means pretty; here it means bringing things back, which is what a retriever is bred to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden retriever is a gun-dog breed trained to carry back game birds to the shooter.

clue.text: Dots measure between street's start and finish

indicators.note: one piece is set between two others, which close round it
the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: a peck is an old dry measure, a quarter of a bushel

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its closing letter only

parts.note: the closing letter, the possessive s

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking out points along a road from one end to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The finish of 'street's' is the S of the possessive, not the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Specks are tiny spots or particles, the same thing as small dots.

clue.text: Note judged to have sounded harsh

explanation.surface: A musical note was assessed and found to be jarring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grated made a rasping, unpleasant noise that set the listener's teeth on edge.

clue.text: Demonstrate in favour of exam

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

explanation.surface: Students march in support of keeping an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrate' looks like 'show', but here it is to march or object publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to hold a public demonstration objecting to something.

clue.text: Preview of film featuring drag queen

parts.note: to trail something is to drag it behind
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: An advert for a movie that stars a drag performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' reads as one phrase, but the two words are clued separately, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a short promotional clip showing scenes from a forthcoming movie.

clue.text: Fire exit?

parts.note: surface reading: an escape door from a burning building
setter's reading: departure from life, by way of flames

explanation.walkthrough: Exit can mean death, so a fire exit is leaving this world by being burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation is the disposal of a dead body by burning, a final departure through flames.

clue.text: Typically first-rate design gives pleasure

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew
first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Good design, as a rule, brings delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-rate' looks like one word meaning excellent; the hyphen hides that 'first' belongs to 'Typically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is something that brings special delight, so it stands as a noun for pleasure.

clue.text: Suddenly start to look lively

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: to pry is to look nosily

explanation.surface: Someone jumps with a start and begins to appear energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suddenly start' reads as a jolt, but start applies only to the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, often elderly, who is active and nimble, the same as lively.

clue.text: Continued with return to theatre, having made a break

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: severed means cut off or broke

explanation.surface: An actor came back to the stage after an interval away.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory theatre, rep for short, is a company staging a rotating set of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, so persevered matches continued as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Disreputable house has broken doorbell

indicators.note: a broken thing is smashed apart, so its letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A seedy house with a doorbell that does not work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordello is a brothel, the kind of establishment politely called a house of ill repute.

clue.text: Savile Row worker and crazy dame are perfectly suited

parts.note: Savile Row in London is famous for bespoke tailoring

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the word after it is scrambled

explanation.surface: A London tailor and an eccentric lady make an ideal match.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is the London street of high-end made-to-measure suit makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailor-made means made to fit exactly, so figuratively ideal or perfectly suited to a purpose.

clue.text: First try, then reject, type of tobacco — it's awful!

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the next word
to reject is to throw back, so the word is sent back to front

parts.note: a cigar is rolled tobacco leaf

explanation.surface: Someone tries a cigar, spits it out and declares it horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic in loose use means dreadful or deplorable, a common informal sense of awful.

clue.text: Matt and Sue worked to make changes

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the names are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: Two colleagues collaborated to bring about some alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form or nature, so mutates works as the verb changes.

clue.text: Game girl — graduate — returned with nothing and left with nothing

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a stock crossword girl

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the graduate's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A young woman graduate comes home penniless and leaves the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a two-headed spinning top is tossed on a string between sticks.

clue.text: Neat arrangement for volatile spot

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a chosen order, here a different order of the letters

explanation.surface: A tidy flower display set out for a lively place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile' sounds like a temper; here it means liable to erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a place prone to sudden eruptions.

clue.text: Executioner to get rid of servant

parts.note: to axe something is to cut or scrap it

explanation.surface: A headsman is told to sack a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: An axeman is one who wields an axe, historically the headsman who beheaded condemned prisoners.

clue.text: Felt pain with dreadful head cold

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the word is muddled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone suffering through a heavy cold in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to suffer a dull continuous hurt, so ached is the past tense meaning felt pain.

clue.text: Happen to disturb terrapins

indicators.note: to disturb is to stir up, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles upon and bothers some turtles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happen to' reads as 'chance to'; the definition is Happen alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpire, in its common modern sense, means to occur or take place.

clue.text: Form of exercise: it's developed at university

indicators.note: something developed is worked into a new form, so the word's letters change places

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A type of workout said to have been invented on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a gym exercise raising the torso from lying to sitting, working the stomach muscles.

clue.text: Blink to find a slip of the pen

indicators.note: the letters must be worked over to find the answer, a loose signal to reorder them

explanation.surface: Someone blinks and so spots an error in their writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak; 'to' serves as fodder, and 'slip' in the definition also hints at letters slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkblot is a spill of ink from a pen, a literal slip that leaves a mark on the page.

clue.text: Endless vacation's wrong for a girl

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the word, with its possessive read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A holiday that never finishes turns out badly for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of vacation's stands for 'is', joining the deletion to its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword usage.

clue.text: Who's out to plug theatrical tour de force?

indicators.note: out means disordered or off, so the word before it has its letters muddled

parts.note: a stopper is a plug or bung

explanation.surface: Asking who is going out to publicise a stunning stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a number so brilliant the audience's applause halts the performance.
